speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing knee pain after increasing your physical activity. To help me pinpoint the cause, could you describe exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the history of repetitive pivoting and twisting during volleyball, have you heard a "pop" sound when the pain started, and is the knee currently swollen or unstable?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)

The pain location you described—medial tibia just below the kneecap—strongly suggests stress on the tibial insertion of the soleus or flexor hallucis longus muscles. Given your recent increase in physical activity and history of weight loss attempts, this is consistent with overuse. Have you noticed any bruising on the medial aspect of your lower leg, or does pressing directly on the tibia elicit sharp pain?
